summary.title: Intern-S1-Pro: Scientific Multimodal Foundation Model at Trillion Scale

setting_and_object.category: Architecture (trillion-parameter multimodal foundation model / system report)

details: Scientific domains are far more heterogeneous than natural language (domain-specific notations, long-tailed knowledge), so a scientific foundation model needs far greater capacity while keeping general text/vision ability; naively scaling MoE post-training destabilizes training via expert load imbalance and under-trained routers.
Intern-S1-Pro: a 1T-parameter (A22B activated) scientific multimodal MoE model obtained by expert expansion of Intern-S1, plus multimodal (vision, time-series) encoders.

Core architectural crux: a Grouped Router that partitions experts into G device-aligned groups and picks top-(K/G) within each group, guaranteeing exact cross-device load balance; expansion initializes each group with the pre-expansion Top-1/Top-2 (well-trained) experts.
Straight-through estimator on routing weights so every router embedding receives gradient each pass while the forward pass stays exactly sparse Top-K.
1T total / 22B activated params, Top-k=8 with 8 groups under EP8 expert parallelism; experts initialized from Intern-S1.
Native-resolution ViT vision encoder trained contrastively on ~300M image-text pairs (CC12M, LAION-COCO, SBU, LAION-2B-Multi, Wukong) with MLP projector.
Fourier Position Encoding (FoPE) replacing/augmenting RoPE; time-series module with adaptive subsampling handling 10^0-10^6 time steps across astronomy, geoscience, EEG/ECG, bioacoustics.
6T tokens of continued pre-training on text and image-text data.

PDF-based scientific caption pipeline: MinerU2.5 layout parsing and sub-figure cropping, pHash dedup, topic routing to InternVL3.5-241B (scientific) or a CapRL-trained Qwen2.5-VL-32B (general), plus a 0.5B text-quality filter, yielding ~270B tokens of dense scientific image-text captions.

Conflict mitigation between scientific and general corpora: template/task-form transformation of structured data (e.g., PubChem), prompt diversification and rollout-generated reasoning chains, and system-prompt isolation.

FP8 quantization limited to expert linear layers, BF16 elsewhere, FP32 LM head; operator-level precision alignment between LMDeploy rollout and XTuner training for RMSNorm, router softmax, positional embeddings.
Rollout router replay (expert indices recorded per token/layer and replayed in training, transferred via Ray object refs).
IcePop-style REINFORCE with dual importance ratios (train/rollout and new/old) and masking of tokens with out-of-range ratios; leave-one-out advantage baseline.
Toolkits: OpenCompass, VLMEvalKit, AgentCompass; separate thinking (65k tokens, temp 0.8) and non-thinking (32k, temp 0) configs.
Scientific benchmarks: SciReasoner, SFE, SmolInstruct, MatBench, Mol-Instructions, MicroVQA, Biology-Instruction, XLRS-Bench, MSEarth-MCQ; SciTS subset for time series.
General benchmarks: MMMU-Pro, MMLU-Pro, AIME-2025, IMO-Answer-Bench, RefCOCO, IFBench, OCRBench V2, SArena, LiveCodeBench V6, GAIA, tau^2-Bench, ScreenSpot V2.
Baselines: Qwen3-VL-235B-Thinking, Kimi-K2.5, GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro (plus GPT-4.1-mini, Gemini2.5-Flash, DeepSeek-V3, GPT-5-mini for time series) and the specialized Biology-Instruction model.

key_findings.finding: The trillion-scale model leads proprietary frontier models by large margins on specialized scientific benchmarks while staying competitive on general tasks.
key_findings.evidence: SciReasoner 55.5 vs 14.7 (Gemini-3-Pro) and 13.6 (GPT-5.2); top scores on SmolInstruct 74.8, MatBench 72.8, Mol-Instructions 48.8, Biology-Instruction 52.5, XLRS-Bench 52.8; general results include MMLU-Pro 86.6, AIME-2025 93.1, RefCOCO-avg 91.9, tau^2-Bench 80.9, ScreenSpot V2 93.6, though it trails on LCB V6 (74.3) and MMMU-Pro (72.8).

key_findings.finding: Expert-expansion initialization matters critically: replicating well-trained Top-1/Top-2 experts across groups is stable, whereas spreading differentiated Top-1..Top-8 experts collapses training.
key_findings.evidence: On a 30B-A3B model over 2000 steps, the Top-1/Top-2 replication scheme slightly outperformed the pre-expansion model, while the differentiated assignment dropped performance by over 20 points.

key_findings.finding: A jointly trained large generalist can surpass a domain-specialized model trained on the same biological data.
key_findings.evidence: Against Biology-Instruction on 21 biological sequence tasks with identical underlying data (only text fluency upgraded), average score 52.45 vs 39.24, with extremes such as Protein-Fluorescence 78.14 vs 2.57 and Protein-FunctionEC 72.70 vs 19.79; the specialist still wins on a few tasks (e.g., RNA-NoncodingRNAFamily 63.09 vs 34.50).

key_findings.finding: The mixed-precision RL stabilization stack makes FP8 RL for trillion-scale sparse MoE behave like BF16 training.
key_findings.evidence: On a 30B MoE, FP8 validation accuracy curves track the BF16 baseline throughout optimization and the train-rollout log-probability KL stays controlled, with router replay enforcing identical expert selection between engines.
